primary_diagnosis_treated: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) secondary to post‑MI remodeling, hypertension, obesity, stage 5 CKD and mixed alcoholic/metabolic liver disease

medications.purpose: Secondary cardiovascular prevention after myocardial infarction
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG180 – antiplatelet therapy for secondary prevention

medications.purpose: Dual antiplatelet therapy post‑PCI for STEMI
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG180 – P2Y12 inhibitor after PCI

medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to target HR <70 bpm, review 6 monthly
medications.purpose: Beta‑blockade for post‑MI remodeling and HFpEF
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 – beta‑blocker for chronic heart failure

medications.duration: Lifelong – titrate to maximum tolerated dose, review 2 weekly after changes
medications.purpose: ACE‑I for HF remodeling, hypertension and renal protection
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 – ACE‑I first‑line in heart failure

medications.duration: Hold until liver function repeats; then reassess
medications.purpose: Lipid lowering for secondary prevention (currently held due to severe hyperbilirubinaemia)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 – statin for established CVD

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily (titrate up to 40 mg BID based on volume status)
medications.duration: Start now, titrate to symptom control, then lifelong – review after 2 weeks
medications.purpose: Relieve volume overload in HFpEF with severe CKD
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG106 – loop diuretic for fluid overload in heart failure

medications.dose: 0.25 mg subcutaneous once weekly, titrate to 0.5 mg after 4 weeks
medications.duration: Ongoing – review HbA1c and weight at 3 months, then 6 monthly
medications.purpose: Improve glycaemic control, promote weight loss and reduce CV risk in pre‑diabetes/obesity
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG28 – GLP‑1 RA for pre‑diabetes/obesity with high CV risk

medications.purpose: High‑intensity lipid lowering for secondary prevention (initiate after LFTs normal)
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG181 – high‑intensity statin for established CVD

medications.duration: Lifelong – review BP in 4 weeks and adjust as needed
medications.purpose: Add‑on antihypertensive if BP >140/90 mmHg despite ACE‑I and beta‑blocker
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG136 – CCB as second‑line antihypertensive in CKD

medications.dose: 800 mg orally three times daily with meals
medications.duration: Lifelong – review phosphate, calcium, PTH in 3 months
medications.purpose: Control hyperphosphataemia in stage 5 CKD (if labs confirm)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 – phosphate binders for CKD‑MBD

medications.duration: Until haemoglobin >10 g/dL, then reassess every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat CKD‑related anaemia (if Hb <10 g/dL and iron replete)
medications.nice_justification: NICE NG203 – ESA therapy for CKD anaemia with adequate iron stores

interactions_checked.interaction: Concurrent use increases risk of myopathy and rhabdomyolysis
interactions_checked.action: Discontinue simvastatin and allow 48 h washout before starting atorvastatin

interactions_checked.interaction: Additive hypotensive and renal effects; may cause electrolyte disturbances
interactions_checked.action: Start furosemide at low dose, monitor BP, electrolytes and renal function after each titration

interactions_checked.interaction: Potential for symptomatic hypotension and worsening renal function
interactions_checked.action: Monitor blood pressure and renal function closely

interactions_checked.interaction: Sevelamer can bind enalapril and reduce its absorption
interactions_checked.action: Take enalapril at least 1 hour before or 2 hours after sevelamer with meals
Monitor for signs of bleeding; routine labs every 3 months
Check BP after initiation and adjust doses if symptomatic hypotension occurs

contraindications.reason: eGFR 8.7 mL/min/1.73 m² – contraindicated due to risk of lactic acidosis (NICE NG28)
eGFR <20 mL/min/1.73 m² – below threshold for efficacy and safety (NICE NG28)
contraindications.alternative: None; focus on loop diuretic and GLP‑1 RA

contraindications.reason: CKD stage 5 – would worsen renal function and fluid retention (NICE NG106)
Ineffective at eGFR <30 and may cause electrolyte imbalance (NICE NG106)
Fluid retention worsens heart failure (NICE NG106)
Severe hyperbilirubinaemia suggests active liver disease; statins contraindicated until LFTs normal (NICE CG181)
contraindications.alternative: PCSK9 inhibitor (evolocumab 140 mg SC q2 weeks) if liver disease persists

assumptions_warnings: Blood pressure not recorded – NICE NG136 requires BP measurement before adding/amending antihypertensives.
Serum potassium not available – needed before up‑titrating ACE‑I or considering MRA/ESA.
Liver function tests (ALT, AST, GGT, INR) not repeated – required before restarting any statin (CG181).
Serum phosphate, calcium and PTH not available – required before initiating sevelamer (NG203).
Iron studies (Ferritin, TSAT) and haemoglobin not confirmed – needed before ESA therapy (NG203).
Exact left ventricular ejection fraction not documented – would influence choice of ARNI vs ACE‑I (NG106).
Vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal, COVID‑19) unknown – NICE recommends annual vaccination for HF and CKD patients.
Allergy history not provided – verify no allergy to GLP‑1 RA, statins, or PCSK9 inhibitors.
Patient’s alcohol intake quantity not quantified – needed for hepatology referral and safe dosing of hepatically cleared drugs.
treatment_summary: The plan addresses HFpEF with volume overload (furosemide), optimises secondary cardiovascular prevention (hold simvastatin, start high‑intensity atorvastatin after LFTs or use PCSK9 inhibitor), treats pre‑diabetes/obesity (semaglutide), and manages CKD complications (conditional sevelamer, ESA). Blood pressure control is refined with possible amlodipine, and all drug choices follow NICE NG106, NG136, CG181, NG28 and NG203. Interactions and contraindications have been reviewed, and key missing investigations are flagged for completion before finalising conditional therapies.
